item.title: Crystal 1.22.2 is released!
item.author: Crys
item.content:encoded: We are announcing a new Crystal release 1.22.2. This release contains no source changes and is only a package increment. It was necessary in order to maintain compatibility of the bundled libgc.a library.

item.title: [ANN] odf v0.1.0: Pure-Crystal OASIS ODF 1.3 .ods reader and writer, zero dependencies
item.author: renich
item.content:encoded:
I just tagged , a pure-Crystal OASIS OpenDocument Format 1.3 shard built strictly on Crystal’s standard library (, , ) with zero runtime dependencies and zero C wrappers.I needed self-contained static binaries that could generate and parse real spreadsheets with live formulas and proper styling without shelling out to Python or LibreOffice, so I built from the ground up. Writer (Odf::Spreadsheet::Workbook): Multi-sheet workbooks, typed cells (, , , , , , , ), live OpenFormula expressions, cell merges, frozen panes, autofilters, and reusable styles/number formats.Hardened Reader (): XXE-safe XML parsing, streaming Zip-bomb byte quotas, and bounded repeat-cell expansion.Extensible Core (): and are document-agnostic, so adding , , and support does not require touching the container engine.require "odf"
workbook = Odf::Spreadsheet::Workbook.new do |book| book.currency_style("usd", symbol: "$", decimals: 2, negative_red: true)
book.sheet("BOM") do |sheet| sheet.freeze(rows: 1) sheet.header_row(["Qty", "Item", "Unit Price", "Total"])
sheet.row do |row| row.integer(4) row.text("NVMe OSD Node") row.currency(12_500.00, style: "usd") row.formula("=[.A2]*[.C2]", cached: 50_000.00, style: "usd") end end end
workbook.save("bom.ods")
doc = Odf::Spreadsheet::Reader.open("bom.ods") puts doc.sheet("BOM")[1][3].as_f # => 50000.0 If anyone is interested in tackling , , or modules on top of , contributions and feedback are very welcome!

item.title: Fedora 46 Proposal Wants To Provide Official Support For Crystal Programming
item.author: renich
item.content:encoded: A new change proposal that's been filed for evaluation with next year's Fedora 46 release is to provide official, native support for the Crystal programming language.
